visual.title: A positive discriminant can still be a true hyperbola
visual.caption: The equation x² − 0.25y² − 1 = 0 has B² − 4AC = 1, so the discriminant is positive. Its right side is not zero, which keeps the two branches apart. Setting the constant to zero would give the intersecting lines x = ±0.5y instead.

predict.question: For x² − 0.25y² − 1 = 0, why is this a hyperbola rather than two intersecting lines?
options: A positive discriminant always means lines
The x² coefficient is larger than the y² coefficient
The constant −1 keeps the branches away from the centre
predict.explain: A positive discriminant only says the quadratic part has opposite signs. The constant term −1 moves the two branches away from the centre. If the constant were zero, the equation would factor into the two lines x = ±0.5y.
